scope: Acceptance contracts for the existing 13 AS1/AS2/AS3/AS4/OFTP2/PeSIT baseline rows. No runtime support, conformance, vendor comparison or whole journey is qualified.
normative_scope: All applicable named-profile requirements remain mandatory. Listed cases are minimum acceptance cases, not a replacement for the full specification or GOAL.md.

C-SCOPE.description: Use two tenants and two partners; refuse unauthorized identities, file/path/receipt lookup, recovery and agent-tool access through every implemented surface.

C-DURABLE.description: Crash before and after acknowledged persistence. Reconcile bytes, immutable revision, event, intent and receipt; refuse partial, quarantined or unverified publication.

C-RETRY.description: Race identical operation identities, lose committed responses and restart. Preserve the original result without repeating business effects; refuse changed meaning.

C-AUTHORITY.description: Change credentials, destination/trust, approval and policy after review and while queued; recheck current authority and retain ambiguous outcomes.

C-BOUNDS.description: Fix and measure byte/header/part/depth, memory/temp-storage, admission, deadline, queue and retry limits before parsing adversarial or expanded input.

C-RECEIPT.description: Verify the strongest promised receipt against exact message/file/peer identities. A transport acknowledgment alone cannot establish downstream business acceptance.

C-PEER.description: Pin an independently implemented sender/receiver build and configuration; retain actual received bytes, checksums, native output, failures and reproducible steps.

C-SURFACES.description: Exercise the shared typed workflow and permissions through browser/API/CLI; replay ordinary transfer and recovery with AI disabled.

AS1-SECURITY.description: Verify signed/encrypted mail and the selected MIME/security combination with independent peer bytes; malformed or substituted content must not publish.
AS1-SECURITY.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

AS1-MDN.description: Correlate signed positive/negative receipts; test relay acceptance followed by missing, forged, delayed or duplicate receipts.
AS1-MDN.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

AS1-ROTATION.description: Rotate trust/credentials with queued mail and late receipts; preserve original receipt identity and visible uncertainty.
AS1-ROTATION.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

AS2-MDN.description: Verify signed/encrypted messages and sync/async signed MDNs against original identity, MIC and signer.
AS2-MDN.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

AS2-RETRY.description: Lose a committed reply; repeat identical content, Date and Message-ID. Recover its receipt; refuse changed-content ID reuse.
AS2-RETRY.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

AS2-NEGATIVE.description: Refuse malformed messages, wrong bindings, negative MDNs and missing/late callbacks.
AS2-NEGATIVE.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

AS2-ROLLOVER.description: Test reviewed certificate rollover during retries/late callbacks, preserving original message/receipt identity.
AS2-ROLLOVER.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

AS3-MDN.description: Verify CMS/MIME and signed MDNs over the selected FTP carrier; correlate the exact original message and digest.
AS3-MDN.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

AS3-INTERRUPT.description: Interrupt file upload and receipt retrieval; stage complete bytes, recover the exact transfer and refuse changed-content ID reuse.
AS3-INTERRUPT.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

AS3-CARRIER.description: Test the selected FTP security, data channels and completion/rename contract independently; an ordinary FTP client alone cannot establish AS3 semantics.
AS3-CARRIER.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

AS4-ROLES.description: Test Push/Pull in all initiating/responding roles and enforce channel authority.
AS4-ROLES.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

AS4-RECEIPTS.description: Test response/callback and bundled receipt handling against original signed message parts.
AS4-RECEIPTS.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

AS4-SECURITY.description: Refuse wrapping, changed attachments, forged receipts and unauthorized Pull before publication.
AS4-SECURITY.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

AS4-RECOVERY.description: Detect missing receipts; recover identical retries after reply loss and restart without changing signed digests.
AS4-RECOVERY.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

OFTP2-SECURITY.description: Verify selected session authentication and signed/encrypted file profile with an independent peer; refuse invalid identities and modified bytes.
OFTP2-SECURITY.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

OFTP2-RESTART.description: Negotiate restart, interrupt transmission and resume exact immutable bytes; qualify record/offset semantics and reject changed source or unauthorized continuation.
OFTP2-RESTART.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

OFTP2-RESPONSE.description: Correlate EERP/NERP to the exact file and origin/destination; validate required signed response. RTR alone cannot mark end-to-end delivery.
OFTP2-RESPONSE.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

PESIT-CONTRACT.description: Select the exact permitted specification/version, security/receipt/restart profile and independent client/server before claiming support.
PESIT-CONTRACT.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case

PESIT-EXCHANGE.description: After selection, independently verify send/receive, interruption/restart, integrity, duplicate identity and positive/negative response semantics.
PESIT-EXCHANGE.source: GOAL.md plus named specification; freightctl minimum acceptance case
